correctness.rationale: For N=3^k, k≥2, the exact generating function gives M_(N−3)=−(1/2)[x^(N−1)]sqrt((1+x)(1−3x)). The binomial identity binom(1/2,t)=(-1)^(t−1)2C_(t−1)/4^t makes all j≥k terms 3-adically zero. For 1≤j<k, setting s=N−j−2, Kummer carry formula gives ν3(C_s)=carries_3(s+s)−ν3(s+1)≥k−j. This is established by explicit ternary digits at j=1,2,3 and for j≥4 by selecting r with 3^(r−1)<j+2≤3^r, obtaining at least k−r carries and ν3(j+1)≤r−1, with 2r≤j. Thus only j=0 remains. The exact Catalan identity C_(N−2)=N binom(2N,N)/[4(2N−1)(2N−3)], Lucas binom(2N,N)≡2 mod3, and 3/(2N−3)≡−1 mod3 yield C_(N−2)/4^(N−1) ≡−3^(k−1) mod3^k. The coefficient is exactly nonzero mod3^k, so ν3(M_(3^k−3))=k−1. Boundary k=2 works; no claim about all indices or 3-regularity. Independent private integer recurrence checked k=2..7 (n=6,24,78,240,726,2184), with residues 6,18,54,162,486,1458; independent ternary carry inequality checked 66 instances through k=12. Such finite tests corroborate the unrestricted proof, not replace it.
residual_risks: The unboundedness proof is exact on n=3^k−3, not a formula for arbitrary n or a proof of 3-regularity.
The Kummer/Lucas normalization is crucial; finite calculations are not unrestricted formal certification.

value.rationale: The ordinary Motzkin sequence is a canonical combinatorial/arithmetic object. The exact nonzero residue and growing valuation on natural ternary indices 3^k−3 resolves the unboundedness half of a named published open question, not merely a finite check or routine renamed example. The precise valuation k−1 is useful for prime-power congruences and distinguishes the unanswered regularity question; the proof adds a concrete structural Catalan carry mechanism.
residual_risks: It settles only unboundedness, not 3-regularity or the general valuation sequence.
